decisions.reason: A directly addresses B as 'Mrs. White' in turns 1 and 7; explicit naming.
Turn 3 states 'Mr. Cooper, your manager' where 'your' refers to B; explicit relational fact.
'B's name is Mrs. White' is equivalent to 'B is named Mrs. White' in c1; c1 has stronger E1 source.

decisions.claim: B works at a location where Mr. Cooper is the manager
decisions.reason: 'B works at a location where Mr. Cooper is the manager' is a weaker presuppositional projection of c2's explicit 'Mr. Cooper is B's manager.'

decisions.claim: B did something helpful for A regarding seeing Mr. Cooper
decisions.reason: A's 'Thanks a lot' in turn 7 presupposes B did something helpful regarding the request to see Mr. Cooper; genuine E2 inference from gratitude.

decisions.claim: B is addressed with the title 'Mrs.'
decisions.reason: 'B is addressed with the title Mrs.' is a weaker projection of c1's full claim that B is named Mrs. White.
'Mrs.' title presupposes female gender; this is a genuine E2 presupposition not captured by c1's name claim alone.

decisions.claim: B has the ability or role to facilitate A's meeting with Mr. Cooper
decisions.reason: Second-review support: The question 'Can I see Mr. Cooper, your manager now?' presupposes that B (Mrs. White) has the role or ability to facilitate or grant access to Mr. Cooper. This is a standard pragmatic presupposition of such requests directed at a specific person—A would not ask B unless B had some capacity to arrange or permit the meeting. The presupposition is minimal and justified by the question structure itself.
decisions.counterexample: If B were merely a bystander with no connection to Mr. Cooper's scheduling, the question would be pragmatically odd, supporting the presupposition.

decisions.claim: B agreed or responded affirmatively to A's request about seeing Mr. Cooper
decisions.reason: 'All right' in turn 5 is A's own utterance, not B's response; attributing agreement to B is an inferred response not supported by visible turns.
decisions.counterexample: A's 'All right' could be self-acknowledgment or response to an unseen statement.
